name: MGAT2-CDG (CDG-IIa)
aliases: congenital disorder of glycosylation type IIa

reference.source: Scriver's OMMBID / Nelson Textbook of Paediatrics
clinicalPearls: A prototypical N-linked type II CDG caused by deficiency of Golgi N-acetylglucosaminyltransferase II, which blocks conversion of hybrid to complex N-glycans
Presents in infancy with dysmorphism, developmental delay, hypotonia and seizures rather than the peripheral neuropathy and cerebellar hypoplasia characteristic of type I disease
Recurrent infections and a bleeding tendency reflect hypoglycosylation of immune and coagulation proteins
Skeletal and facial dysmorphic features are common, and gastrointestinal problems may occur
Because the defect is in glycan processing, transferrin isoelectric focusing shows a type II pattern (increased mono- and asialotransferrin from truncated antennae)
Management is supportive and multidisciplinary; no specific dietary or enzyme therapy alters the underlying defect
Confirmed by MGAT2 sequencing supported by enzyme assay in leucocytes or fibroblasts
reference.pathophysiology: MGAT2 encodes N-acetylglucosaminyltransferase II, a Golgi enzyme that adds a second N-acetylglucosamine branch during maturation of N-glycans from hybrid to biantennary complex structures. Deficiency arrests processing after the oligosaccharide has already been transferred to protein, so the glycan chains are structurally truncated rather than absent. This defines a type II disorder, distinguishable from type I assembly defects by the transferrin isoform pattern on isoelectric focusing or mass spectrometry. Truncated complex glycans impair function of many secreted and membrane glycoproteins, producing the multisystem phenotype.
additionalDifferentials: Other type II CDG subtypes (e.g. TMEM165-CDG, B4GALT1-CDG, COG-complex CDG, SLC35A2-CDG)
Type I CDG subtypes when the transferrin pattern is ambiguous
Chromosomal and other syndromic causes of dysmorphism with developmental delay
additionalInvestigations: Transferrin isoelectric focusing or mass spectrometry demonstrating a type II pattern
redFlags: Recurrent or severe infections suggesting significant immune dysfunction
Unexplained bleeding from coagulation factor hypoglycosylation
Failure to thrive with multi-organ involvement
reference.prognosis: MGAT2-CDG causes significant and lasting neurodevelopmental disability; life expectancy is variable and depends on the severity of infections, bleeding and other systemic complications. There is no treatment that corrects the enzymatic defect.
pitfalls: Assuming a type II transferrin pattern excludes CDG when the clinical picture differs from classic PMM2-CDG
Failing to distinguish type I from type II defects, which alters the candidate gene list
Overlooking immunodeficiency and bleeding risk in perioperative planning
Interpreting an isolated enzyme result without molecular confirmation
references: Scriver's OMMBID, congenital disorders of glycosylation
Nelson Textbook of Paediatrics, disorders of glycosylation
